result:
I fixed 11 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. All 150 rules now match the docstrings and the module docstring's shared rules.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | The cap was applied to the price, not the discount (`min(base, 30000) * 5 // 100`) | Compute the discount first, then cap it at 30,000 |
| 36 | The 50,000 cap only kicked in when the discount was over 100,000 | Always cap at 50,000 |
| 70 | The 30,000 cap only kicked in when the discount was over 60,000 | Always cap at 30,000 |
| 40 | `qty > 12`, so 12 units got no discount | `qty >= 12` |
| 113 | `qty > 100`, so 100 units got no discount | `qty >= 100` |
| 42 | Labeled marginal but discounted every unit | Discount only units above 30 |
| 63 | Used 9% instead of 8% | 8% |
| 85 | Used 6% instead of 5% | 5% |
| 134 | Used 3% instead of 2% | 2% |
| 137, 140 | Used `round()` (rounding to nearest) | Round down to the won (`//`) |

Rule 82 had its threshold written as `qty >= 51`. The result was the same either way, because the discount at exactly 50 units is 0. I still changed it to `>= 50` to match the docstring.

**How I checked:** I wrote a script that builds the expected price from each docstring (type, %, threshold, cap) using the module's shared rules. It compares that with each function over about 1,900 quantity and unit-price combinations, including each threshold and the points where each cap starts. Before the fix, only the 11 rules above failed. After the fix, none do. There are no tests in this repo, so this script was the only check. It's in the scratchpad, not the repo.

STATUS: DONE
